tagline.text: A hike up a dormant volcano in northern Bataan with a caldera and waterfalls

location.label: Location
location.text: Tala jump-off, Orani, Bataan, in the Bataan Natural Park area of the northern Bataan Peninsula

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: One day (day trip from Manila or an overnight trip)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,100–2,200 (joiner tour or DIY hike, per person)

children.text: Mount Natib is a volcano rising about 1,253–1,287 m in the northern Bataan Peninsula, with a large caldera, hot springs and forest waterfalls. The hike starts at the Tala jump-off in Orani and can be done as a day trip from Manila, but it is an intermediate-to-hard route that requires a guide.

Mount Natib is a stratovolcano and caldera complex in the northern Bataan Peninsula. Sources give its height as 1,253 m (Wikipedia and Bataan tourism material) or 1,287 m (some mountaineering sources). The main caldera measures about 6 by 7 km and opens to the northwest, and to the east lies the smaller Pasukulan Caldera, about 2 km wide. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) classifies it as dormant but "potentially active," and a large eruption roughly 11,000 to 18,000 years ago (a pyroclastic flow found in Subic Bay sediment) is known, though it cannot be taken as the last one and younger eruptions are considered possible.

The mountain's appeal is that forest, rock walls and waterfalls are all in one place. The most common route is the Tala back trail, which climbs from Barangay Tala in Orani. It begins with gentle forest paths and grassland, followed by steep forest and rope sections near the top, and near the summit you can see the white cross on Mount Samat and, on a hazy day, Mount Mariveles. One hiking guide rates the Tala route 4 out of 9 (moderate to major), 5 with Pasukulan Falls added, and 6 for the Orani-to-Morong traverse.

The hike is usually done in one day, leaving Manila before dawn. One guide gives a sample schedule: leave Manila at 3 a.m., register around 6 a.m., start hiking at 6:30, reach the summit between 10:30 and 11:30, begin descending at noon, and be back at the jump-off between 3 and 4 p.m. It says the trip takes about 14.5 hours from Manila back to Manila, so consider your fitness. Adding Pasukulan Falls takes about 21 hours, so an overnight trip is recommended.

The Natib area is a protected zone within Bataan Natural Park, first declared Bataan National Park in 1945. A local guide and registration are practically required, and fees, entry rules and whether camping is allowed change from year to year, so check the latest notices from the Orani municipal office and the Bataan tourism office before you set out.
About
30–45 minutes
from the Tala jump-off you reach the first viewpoint, the Pinagbutasan View Deck. It is a good place to catch your breath for the first rest early in the hike.
About
12–15 minutes

beyond the view deck is a small hut called Kubo House. It is almost the only reliable year-round water source on the main trail, and it is the junction where the path to Pasukulan Falls (straight) and the path to the base camp and summit (left) split. Water is scarce after this, so carry 2–3 L.
About
45 minutes to 1 hour
above Kubo House you reach the large flat grassland base camp. It is used for resting or pitching tents, but whether camping is currently allowed must be confirmed locally.

children.text: The stretch from base camp to the summit takes about
45 minutes to 1.5 hours
and gains about
in elevation. In places you climb near-vertical rock faces 5–10 m high, called the Four Walls, using ropes, so gloves are needed. From the summit you can see the white cross on Mount Samat.
A forest waterfall about
2–3 hours
one way from Kubo House, with views of the stream valley inside the caldera. Guides mention a surcharge of about
on the guide fee, and there is also an approach from the Letran-Abucay side.

Heading west toward Morong from the camp below the summit, you face a descent of 12–14 km. A 2013 trip report passed park-like sections and forested ridges, crossed the Morong River eight times in knee-deep water and came out at Sitio Kanawan, an Aeta village, taking more than seven hours from the summit to the Morong exit. A hut beside the trail reportedly offered hikers sweet potatoes (kamote). A guide is essential and the route demands stamina.
The Natib caldera area has five thermal zones with hot springs, Asin, Mamot, Tigulangin, Uyong and Paipit, with water temperatures of about
. For this reason the area is also a subject of research on geothermal energy and volcanic activity.

items.title: Day hike
items.subtitle: Round trip to the summit on the Tala back trail

children.text: Take a bus bound for Balanga or Mariveles from Manila (Pasay, Cubao or Avenida) and get off at Orani Crossing. If you have a car or van, an early start is much easier.
Take a tricycle from Orani Crossing to Tala. It takes about 25–30 minutes, and guides mention a fare of about
per vehicle.
Register at the hiking outpost in Barangay Tala and set off with your guide.
Pass the Pinagbutasan View Deck and Kubo House, and refill your water.
Pass the grassland base camp and climb to the summit. Summit arrival is given as 10:30 to 11:30.
Finish lunch and photos at the summit and begin the descent.
Return to the Tala jump-off. Descents often run late, so hurry down before dark.
The schedule is an example from a guide and will vary greatly with pace and weather. After rain the trail is slippery and leeches increase, so it is not recommended for beginners.

items.title: With Pasukulan Falls
items.subtitle: An overnight trip at a relaxed pace

children.text: Leave Manila around midnight and arrive in Tala at dawn. One guide says a round trip from Manila including the falls takes about 21 hours.
Register, start hiking with your guide and climb to Kubo House.
Go straight from Kubo House toward Pasukulan Falls. It takes about 2–3 hours one way.
Finish lunch and rest at the falls, then return.
Descend via Kubo House to the Tala jump-off.
Going all the way to the summit as well takes considerable stamina. Arrange camping availability and the guide fee in advance.
Take a Genesis or Bataan Transit bus from Cubao, Pasay or Avenida toward Balanga or Mariveles and get off at Orani Crossing.
A 2013 trip report says the Genesis bus fare was ₱187 and the ride took about 2.5 hours. Fares change, so confirm locally.

items.title: End of the traverse and the return

children.text: The Orani-to-Morong traverse ends at Sitio Kanawan in Morong. From there, one route described returns to Manila via Subic and Olongapo.
A traverse needs transport arranged in advance, so talk to your guide or tour operator.
Do not count on cards or mobile payments near the jump-off, and bring plenty of small bills.
The dry season from November to April is the most reliable time to hike. The trail is less slippery and stream water is relatively safe.
In the June–October rainy season leeches increase, and rock walls and mossy rocks are slippery when wet. Beginners should not climb right after heavy rain.
An early start is the rule. Descents often take longer than expected and end after dark.

The hike itself is a day trip, so many people do not book lodging, but if an early start is hard you can stay the night before in Balanga or Orani town. Balanga, the provincial capital, has lodging and restaurants close together and is convenient.
There are no shops on the mountain, so bring trail food, lunch and plenty of water. After the hike, restaurants in Orani or Balanga are good places for Filipino home cooking.
Cost estimates differ widely between sources. One source calculates about
per person for a group of four going on their own and about
for a joiner tour, and advises setting aside
per person as an emergency buffer. The FAQ of the same source gives about
for a DIY hike and about
for a joiner tour, so the numbers conflict. Confirm what is included with the operator before booking.
Treat a guide as mandatory and arrange one at the registration outpost. Guides are arranged at one guide per 7 hikers.
Gloves are essential for the ropes and rock walls.
There is a lot of mud and mossy rock, so wear shoes with good traction.
For leeches (limatik), bring long sleeves and salt or alcohol.
Water is scarce after Kubo House, so carry 2–3 L.
Bring a headlamp, rain jacket, trekking pole, trail food and a trash bag.
Start early so that your descent does not end in the dark.
Cards and mobile payments may not work at the jump-off, so bring small bills.
According to a 2013 trip report, it took about 2.5 hours from Tala to the camp and about 45 minutes from the camp to the summit. This varies with fitness and weather.

Natib is a protected area where a guide and registration are practically required, and fees, entry rules, Pasukulan access and whether camping is allowed change often. Before you go, confirm the latest information with the Orani municipal office and the Bataan tourism office (tel. (047) 935-0364).
This is an intermediate-to-hard hike not recommended for complete beginners. There are rope and rock-wall sections.
After rain the rocks and moss are very slippery and leeches increase.
Descents tend to run late, so leave yourself plenty of daylight to come down.
Water is limited, so be sure to refill at Kubo House.
The traverse involves several crossings of the Morong River, which can be dangerous on rainy days.
One trip report records that the area around the summit was shrouded in haze and Mount Mariveles looked faint. Even if you hope for views, they may not be visible depending on the weather.
A taller volcanic massif in the south of the Bataan Peninsula, famous for the Tarak Ridge hike.
A war memorial shrine whose white cross is visible from the summit. A good stop before or after the hike.
The provincial capital of Bataan, a base town with lodging and restaurants.
A coastal area you can continue to after finishing the Morong-side traverse.
